details: CONFIRMED by reading: rules/front.md:13-14 and rules/delegation.md:24-25 are unchanged on the branch and are the text of
the global CLAUDE.md. The global file says skills override it, so a session that loaded the front skill would follow the
skill; but the front skill's load at session start is advice, not a hook, and the open queue item
the-flow-s-skills-give-a-session-opposite-orders is about exactly this kind of disagreement; the change adds one more.
Note: rules/ is a design-review trigger in the delegate skill's table; the fix is two sentences that restate the decision
already taken, so the owner may waive it. Size: 15.
evidence: git grep -n -E 'waited on in calls|a test run go to a runner' -> rules/delegation.md:25: longer job runs detached with a log,
waited on in calls of at most 240 s. ; rules/front.md:14: issue, a test run go to a runner that replies in 3 lines.
git diff --stat master...HEAD -> no file under rules/.
failing_case: A relay front session after a change that edited skill texts. Its ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (written by relay sync from rules/)
says "a test run go to a runner that replies in 3 lines" (rules/front.md:13-14) and "a longer job runs detached with a log,
waited on in calls of at most 240 s" (rules/delegation.md:24-25). The front skill now says the full paid bin/ci is "never a
runner", "no `&`, no polling". A front that follows the rules (the front skill's load is not enforced) gives the 40-52 min
paid run to a runner again, and the runner runs out of turns mid-wait: the failure this change fixes, a 5th time.
Expected: the rule texts say the same as the skill for a job longer than about 30 minutes.
fix_hint: Add the exception to the two rule bullets (one clause each), extend the new test to assert them, run relay sync.
pass_cases: 1. rules/front.md, the "Large results stay out of the session" bullet, names the exception: a job over about 30 minutes
(the full paid bin/ci) the front starts itself with Bash run_in_background into a scratchpad log and reads only its end.
2. rules/delegation.md, the "No command blocks over 4 minutes" bullet: the 240 s polling applies to agents; a job longer
than an agent's turns cover is started by the front in the background, not polled.
3. After `relay sync`, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md carries both lines (relay sync writes the rules there).
4. The new test in tests/test_relay.py keeps passing; a test asserts the rule lines as it asserts the skill lines.
reason: rules/front.md and rules/delegation.md carry the exception; tests in tests/test_relay.py (Roles long-job test, TestTasteRule rendered-global test) pass.
findings.summary: the rules every session loads still send a test run to a runner and the wait to 240 s polling, opposite to the new front skill

details: CONFIRMED: bin/ci prints one line per step and eval-record's report(); report() builds the head from fails, splits and
unjudged only (bin/eval-record:101-103); the plugin-evals step log of the last full run is 3 lines with no cost; the stored
record has costUsd 9.309. Before this change the instruction "report its cost" did not limit what was read; the new
"read only the log's last lines" makes it unreachable. It recurs on every change that edits skill or rule texts.
Size: 15.
evidence: bin/eval-record:101 head = f"ci: eval record: {...} meaning grader(s) failed, {splits} split vote..."
failing_case: Front runs the full paid bin/ci in the background as the skill now says, is notified, reads the log's last lines:
"ci: plugin evals ok (2837s)", "ci: eval record: 0 meaning grader(s) failed, 0 split votes", "ci: green". The same
paragraph orders "report its cost on the screen": the cost ($9.31 for the native-language run) is only in
.ci/evals.json / ~/.relay/evals/relay/<stamp>.json (costUsd), never printed. The front either breaks "read only the last
lines" (opens a JSON) or leaves the cost off the merge screen.
Expected: the log's last lines carry the cost, e.g. "ci: eval record: $9.31, 0 meaning grader(s) failed, 0 split votes".
fix_hint: Add the cost to report()'s head line when data has costUsd (formatted $x.xx); test it beside the existing report tests.
pass_cases: 1. bin/eval-record on a record with costUsd 9.309 prints a head line holding "$9.31".
2. A record without costUsd (a partial run) prints the head line without a cost and does not fail.
3. The existing grader-tests cases on the head line (fails, splits, not judged) keep their text otherwise.
4. The front skill's sentence names where the cost is read (the eval record line), so "read only the last lines" and
"report its cost" can both be kept.
reason: bin/eval-record report() adds ", cost $x.xx" only for a numeric costUsd; tests/test_eval_record.py test_the_summary_line_ends_with_the_run_cost passes.
findings.summary: the front is told to read only the paid run's last lines and to report its cost, but no line of bin/ci's output holds the cost

details: CONFIRMED: rules/queue.md says "relay queue take to start one in a worktree, relay queue done to close one with its test";
lib/relay_queue.py:700 take() writes the review JSON with Q1 for a fix item; done() (line 770) refuses unless state is
taken by the branch. The item's expected outcome ("should finish and report within its turns") was met by moving the job
off the runner, a front decision recorded in the handover; Q1's checker should judge that. Rule: rules/queue.md.
Waste that repeats (taste): an open fix at the top of the queue is picked again by the next session. Size: 5.
evidence: relay queue show runner-turns-while-waiting -> fix, ip 99, 15m, open
failing_case: master and the branch: .relay/queue/runner-turns-while-waiting.json has "state": "open", "taken_by": "". The handover
names this change as the fix of that item, but `relay queue take` was never run, so no finding Q1 exists for the checker
(the "From queue item" rule that the failing-case test must fail without the fix never applies) and `relay queue done`
cannot run (it refuses an item not taken by the branch). After the merge `relay queue` still lists it first (fix, ip 99),
and the next session picks it up again.
Expected: the item is taken by wt/runner-turns, checked as Q1, and closed with its test before the merge.
fix_hint: Run relay queue take now (it writes Q1 beside this review), have the checker check Q1 with the review, then relay queue done.
pass_cases: 1. `relay queue take runner-turns-while-waiting -C <wt> --findings <review.json>` lands "taken" by wt/runner-turns.
2. The checker's verdict lists Q1 MET at tests/test_relay.py (the new test), and that test fails at the reviewed base
without the skill lines.
3. `relay queue done runner-turns-while-waiting -C <wt> --test tests/test_relay.py::test_a_job_longer_than_a_runner_s_turns_runs_in_the_front_s_background --check <check.json>`
sets state done, closed_by wt/runner-turns.
4. After the merge `relay queue` no longer lists the item as open.
reason: Item taken and closed by relay queue done (c3f9d21); its check check-queue-runner-turns.json has Q1 MET, failing on base.
findings.summary: rules/queue.md: the branch fixes queue item runner-turns-while-waiting without taking it, so its failing case is never checked and it stays open at ip 99 after the merge

details: CONFIRMED from the native-language worktree's .ci/ci.log step lines. Harmless today (the advice is the same), but a front
that expects 47 minutes may think a 52-minute run is stuck. Size: 5.
evidence: grep 'ci: .*ok (' .worktrees/native-language/.ci/ci.log -> plugin evals ok (2197s) / (2300s) / (2837s); library tests
failing_case: The last three full runs: plugin evals alone 2197 s, 2300 s and 2837 s, plus library tests ~128 s, hook tests ~135 s and
~10 s of small steps: about 41, 43 and 52 minutes. The skill says "38-47 minutes". Expected: the range the runs show
(about 40-55 minutes), or no range (only "longer than a runner's turns cover").
fix_hint: Write "about 40-55 minutes" or drop the range.
pass_cases: 1. The front skill's figure covers 52 minutes (the native-language run, 2837 s of evals).
2. The test still finds "full paid `bin/ci`", "never a runner" and "`run_in_background`".
reason: front SKILL.md no longer gives the 38-47 minute range; run_in_background and never a runner remain.
findings.summary: the paid bin/ci is said to take 38-47 minutes; the last full runs took about 43-52

details: PLAUSIBLE: depends on whether the front reads the delegate skill before routing (it is told to, not forced). Cheap to add
beside the change. Size: 5.
evidence: sed -n 1,8p plugins/delegate/agents/runner.md -> description: Runs one command, test, pipeline read ... running a test
suite, a build, a deploy script ...; maxTurns: 12
failing_case: runner.md description: "Use for ... running a test suite, a build, a deploy script, or any call whose output is long", with
maxTurns 12 and a limits part that says to wait until the job finishes. A front that picks the agent by its description
(the delegate skill's note is not in the agent's text) hands it the 50-minute paid bin/ci; the runner ends mid-wait.
Expected: the description says a job over about 30 minutes is not a runner's.
fix_hint: Append to the description: "Not for a job over about 30 minutes (the front runs it in the background)."
pass_cases: 1. runner.md's description or base names the bound: a job longer than about 30 minutes is the front's, in the background.
2. relay sync agents leaves the description intact (the description is outside the relay:base region).
reason: plugins/delegate/agents/runner.md description now bounds the job to about 30 minutes.
findings.summary: the runner's own description still invites any test suite or build, with no bound, so a front routing by description gives it the paid run
